raw_response:
I am 60 this year, and I have farmed here in Quzhou for 40 years. I did not study agriculture in school, but I have seen enough seasons to know what works on my own land. I do not like making big changes. Wheat and maize are still my backbone because they are steady and the land is already set up for that. Cotton brings cash if the year is smooth, and watermelon can sell well, but both need more watching, so I only keep smaller areas for them. Some people in my family work outside, so I cannot depend on a lot of labor at home every day. I have a well, so I will use irrigation when the crop really needs it, but pumping costs money, so I will not water blindly.

On the wheat-maize land, I will keep doing the usual double crop because it spreads risk. Wheat needs a good base fertilizer and a couple of key irrigations, especially before winter and around jointing if the soil is dry. After wheat harvest, the maize must go in quickly, so I will keep tillage simple and not waste time. For cotton, I will not push fertilizer too hard because too much vegetative growth can be troublesome, and cotton already takes more management for pests and picking. Watermelon can make money, but seed and disease control cost more, so I will keep only a small piece and manage it carefully. I am aiming for a stable year, not gambling for the very highest yield.
